guided.title: A star triangle
guided.prompt: Use nested loops to print a triangle of stars with 4 rows: row 1 has 1 star, row 2 has 2 stars, up to row 4 with 4 stars. Print each star followed by nothing (use `end=""`) and end each row with an empty `print()`.
hints: The outer loop chooses the row number; the inner loop repeats once per star in that row.
The inner loop count equals the row number: `range(row)`.
After the inner loop (one indent less), call `print()` to end the line.

guided.title: Row totals
guided.prompt: `table` is `[[2, 4], [10, 20, 30], [5]]`. For each row print its total on one line, using an inner loop with an accumulator that restarts for every row.
hints: You need an outer loop over rows and an inner loop over the values of one row.
Set `total = 0` inside the outer loop, before the inner loop.
Print `total` once per row, after the inner loop, at the outer level.

guided.title: Filter the emails
guided.prompt: `emails` is `["a@x.com", "bad.address", "b@y.org", "no-at-sign", "c@z.net"]`. Build a new list `valid` of the emails that contain `"@"`, and print `valid` and then the number of invalid ones.
guided.solution:
emails = ["a@x.com", "bad.address", "b@y.org", "no-at-sign", "c@z.net"]
valid = []
for email in emails:
    if "@" in email:
        valid.append(email)
print(valid)
print(len(emails) - len(valid))
hints: Start with an empty list before the loop.
Test `"@" in email` and append only the passing ones.
The number of invalid emails is the original length minus the valid length.

guided.title: Largest of negatives
guided.prompt: `changes` is `[-8, -3, -15, -6]`. Find the largest value using the pattern with `best = None`, not by calling `max()`. Print it.
hints: Start with `best = None`, because 0 would be larger than every item here.
The condition is `best is None or c > best`.
Inside the `if`, set `best = c`; print after the loop.

independent.title: Pairs that add up
independent.prompt: `nums` is `[1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9]`. Print every pair of two different numbers `(a, b)` with `a` before `b` in the list whose sum is 10, one per line in the format `1 + 9`. Use nested loops with `range(len(nums))` and index positions so that each pair appears once.

independent.title: Order lines with prices
independent.prompt: `orders` is `[{"id": 1, "items": ["pen", "ink"]}, {"id": 2, "items": ["paper"]}, {"id": 3, "items": ["pen", "cover", "ink"]}]` and `prices` is `{"pen": 2, "ink": 5, "paper": 4}`. For each order compute the total price, using `prices.get(item, 0)` so unknown items cost 0. Print `Order 1: 7` style lines, one per order, then a final line `Unknown items: ` followed by the sorted list of distinct item names that were not in `prices`.

independent.title: Match students to classes (stretch)
independent.prompt: `students` is `[{"name": "Ada", "class_id": 2}, {"name": "Bo", "class_id": 5}, {"name": "Cy", "class_id": 1}]` and `classes` is `[{"id": 1, "room": "A1"}, {"id": 2, "room": "B7"}]`. For each student find the room by searching `classes` with an inner loop and `break`, defaulting to `"TBC"`. Print `Ada: B7` style lines, in student order. Then print `Missing rooms: ` followed by the number of students whose room is `"TBC"`.
independent.expected:
Ada: B7
Bo: TBC
Cy: A1
Missing rooms: 1

checks.explanation: The inner loop makes 4 passes for each of the 3 outer passes, so 3 times 4 equals 12. The counts multiply; they are not added.
`break` stops only the inner loop, so for each `i` only `j == 0` prints. The outer loop still makes both passes.

checks.question: A programmer finds the maximum of `[-4, -9, -2]` with `best = 0` and the usual comparison. What result do they get?
checks.explanation: No item is greater than 0, so `best` is never replaced and stays 0, which is not even in the list. Start with `None` or the first item.

checks.question: Where must `total = 0` go to get one total per row of a table?
options: Inside the outer loop, before the inner loop
checks.explanation: The total must restart for each row, so it belongs in the outer loop's block before the inner loop. Before the outer loop it would keep adding across rows; inside the inner loop it would reset on every cell.

checks.question:
After the loops below, what is `result`?

```python
result = []
for x in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    if x % 2 == 0:
        result.append(x * 10)
```
checks.explanation: Only the even numbers pass the test, and each is multiplied by 10 before being appended, giving `[20, 40]`.
